newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-LATE GOALS SEND MILAN CRASHING TO DEFEAT IN GOTHENBURG.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-LATE GOALS SEND MILAN CRASHING TO DEFEAT IN GOTHENBURG.

text.p: AC Milan, bidding for a record-equalling sixth European Cup victory, crashed to a shock 2-1 Champions' League defeat at IFK Gothenburg on Wednesday after leading with only 16 minutes to play.

It was Milan's second defeat in three matches in Group D and left them level on only three points with Rosenborg and Gothenburg. Porto, who won 1-0 at Rosenborg, top the group with a maximum nine points.

Milan seemed set for victory after Liberian George Weah put them ahead after 52 minutes but late goals from substitute Erik Walhstedt after 74 minutes and Niclas Alexandersson six minutes from time gave the Swedish champions a shock win and their first victory in the group.
Porto chalked up their third successive win thanks to a last minute goal from Brazilian striker Jardel against a Rosenborg side who had Jan Ivar Jakobsen sent off in the second half.
Dutch champions Ajax rekindled their hopes of reaching a third successive European Cup final when they beat 10-man Glasgow Rangers 4-1 in a Group A match in Amsterdam.

Two goals from Portuguese striker Dani, who does not turn 20 until next month, put the 1995 European champions on their way to victory against Rangers who had England midfielder Paul Gascoigne sent off after 29 minutes for kicking Ajax defender Winston Bogarde.

Nigerian striker Tijani Babangida made it 3-0 seven minutes from time, and although Ian Durrant pulled one back for Rangers with two minutes to go, Ajax added a fourth through Nordin Wooter a minute from time.

The defeat was Rangers' third in three matches and means they are effectively eliminated. Ajax's win put the Dutch champions top of Group A level on six points with Auxerre, who beat Grasshopper Zurich 1-0.
Borussia Dortmund moved clear at the Top of Group B by ending Atletico Madrid's 100 percent record with a 1-0 win in Spain. Stefan Reuter scored the only goal after 50 minutes.
In the other Group B match Steaua Bucharest kept their slender hopes of qualifying alive with a 1-0 win over Widzew Lodz thanks to an own goal from Widzew's Daniel Bogusz eight minutes from time.

European champions Juventus stayed top of Group C despite being held to a 1-1 draw at Rapid Vienna. Christian Vieri gave the Italians the lead in the ninth minute while Polish striker Andrzej Lesiak equalised for the home side 11 minutes later.

Manchester United ended their miserable recent away record in Europe which had produced just one win in the last five years with a 2-0 win over Fenerbahce in Istanbul. David Beckham scored after 55 minutes and Frenchman Eric Cantona added a second five minutes later.
United's victory closed the gap on Juventus to a point and should ensure Juventus and Manchester United a place in the last eight.
